construct: RULED, THE K2 CELL (refreshed 2026-09-21): k2_overview 40–70w (the persona's current in the element's arena) + k2_functional ≤22w (the god's own family function, re-ruled 2026-09-01) + k2_domain_readings 18–55w per ruled domain (owner construct 2026-08-19, corpus ×50 LOCKED) · adj_chips {catalyst ×3, friction ×3} 1–3w under THE KEYWORD DERIVATION CHAIN (2026-09-03) and THE VOCABULARY ZONE B1–B2 (2026-09-04) · fn_reading = the weighted three-door ledger {word, doors:{trait, scene, outside}} ×3 per pole, 35–55w per door (THE THREE DOORS 2026-09-03; corpus ×50 complete 2026-09-04) · structural_interaction = the REA_03 §4b authoring seed · k2_card = the unauthored register stub (REA_03 §4, superseded by the cell above). Prompts: REA_17 §3.4. · edge (catalyst pole only; owner 2026-10-16, THE EDGE v9: two sentences, the energy and its three ruling domains from the GOD table, then a clause per domain in The Pattern's voice; the metric; the head derived in the app)

candidates.structural_interaction: Wood setting standard for Earth cross-polarity — movement asking whether stability is living
candidates.k2_overview: Your Wood moves as the Magistrate: living order that grows. You build careers and codes like trellises, principled frames that help everything on them climb. Authority suits you when it nurtures. People accept your rules because your rules have leaves. Prune the dead ones each season and the frame stays believed in.
candidates.k2_functional: Order is your native climate: you grow straight inside good structure and warp without it.

k2_domain_readings.Career: Your career grows like a managed forest: steady rings, widening responsibility, roots deepening in one good house. Choose organizations you would plant a decade in. Transplanting yearly wastes your kind of compounding.
k2_domain_readings.Status: Your standing grows organically: respect accruing ring by ring until you are somehow the oak everyone consults. Let it. Just keep lower branches reachable.
k2_domain_readings.Order: Your order is cultivated: rules as trellises rather than cages, standards that make growing easier. Systems you design get adopted willingly. Revisit them each season so the living thing never outgrows the frame.

angles.drive: You keep your word long after it stops being convenient. Being counted on is the respect you want, so you put a promise ahead of your comfort. Add your comfort to the promises you keep, because a word kept at any price wears you down.
angles.cost_self: Keeping your word matters more to you than keeping your options. Since breaking a promise feels like losing rank with yourself, you stay inside old plans rather than reopen them. Ask out of one dead promise, and you are free when the next chance comes.
angles.cost_others: Whoever gives you their word, you expect them to keep it. Because you treat a promise as a rule, you count a missed one as a broken rule instead of a bad week. Allow people one free miss, and your word weighs more for it.

angles.drive: You earn every step before you take it. Since a handed rank feels borrowed to you, you earn it twice over rather than ask once. When you ask for the next step a little sooner, you stop working a rank below your worth.
angles.cost_self: Earning every step takes longer than asking for it. Since a rank you never requested sits easier on you, you wait for the title rather than claim it. If you claim what you have earned, you stop losing the title to whoever asked first.
angles.cost_others: Among the people under you, you expect every step to be earned. Since a shortcut looks like cheating, you would rather make them wait than give them a lift. Hand one person a step early, so they spend less time proving what you already know.

angles.drive: You hold the line where letting it slide would be easier. Since you need to know how things stand, you hold the rule ahead of the exception. Let someone else hold one line for a while, instead of carrying every rule alone.
angles.cost_self: Holding the line costs you more than you admit. Since bending a rule feels like losing yourself, you hold it against the people you love as much as against strangers. Bend it once for someone who matters, and you keep a closeness no rule replaces.
angles.cost_others: For everyone, you hold the line, even for those who need an exception. Since one exception feels unfair to the rest, you give the rule in place of a second chance. Weigh what a rule costs someone, to hold the line only where it helps.

angles.drive: You go by the book, even where it was never meant to reach. Since a written rule feels surer than a guess, you go with the book instead of your own judgment. Each time the book decides, you give up a chance to trust yourself.
angles.cost_self: The book spares you the weight of deciding. Since a decision by the rule is never your fault, you follow the book ahead of your own read. Leaving it to the rule, you lose the judgment you never use and the step up it needed.
angles.cost_others: Faced with a person, you reach for the book as much as for a form. Because an exception feels like playing favourites, you hand someone the rule rather than a hearing. Wanting to be fair, you give them a page in place of yourself.

angles.drive: You never bend, whatever the day asks. Because standing firm feels safer to you, you brace against a change of plan rather than lean into it. You stay loyal to the old plan long after it has stopped working.
angles.cost_self: Never bending keeps you honest and keeps you tired. Since a new plan feels like being pushed, you hold your shape instead of saving your strength. You lose every chance that arrives as a change, and you lose it by refusing to bend.
angles.cost_others: Before anyone asks, you make it clear that you never bend. Because a suggested change feels like a push against you, you say no ahead of hearing it out. You leave the people around you holding ideas you never heard.

angles.drive: Rank comes first with you, yours and everyone else's. Because a clear ladder tells you where you stand, you check who is higher up ahead of who is right. Underneath the ranking, you want a safe place more than the right answer.
angles.cost_self: Even when the one being ranked is you, rank comes first. Since a title tells you how well you are doing, you choose rank ahead of liking your work. You keep moving up into jobs you would not pick for the work alone.
angles.cost_others: In how you treat people, rank comes first. Because order feels safer than equals, you give the person above you your best ahead of the one beside you. You send the credit for shared work upward, past your peers.

edge.lead: Wood runs through your family, your social life and your career. It is the word you give at home that everyone leans on, the handshake friends trust more than the paperwork, and the long way up at work while others look for shortcuts.
